title: Silo Line Won't Index
environment: Warehouse — silo fill cell, west bay
briefing: Runs but nothing moves. RUN lamp on, motor humming — and the cartons haven't shifted since 03:00. Nothing flagged on the HMI.

tags.label: STOP_PB
tags.description: Stop pushbutton, momentary NC in field

tags.label: PROX_SENSOR
tags.description: Inductive prox — carton present under silo spout

tags.label: MODE_SEL
tags.description: A/B/C mode selector — declared so the cell's writes land on a real tag; no rung consumes it yet

rungs.description: Start/stop seal-in. RUN latches on START, drops on STOP or E-STOP.
rungs.condition: (I:1/00 OR O:2/02) AND NOT I:1/01 AND NOT I:1/02

rungs.description: Motor runs whenever RUN is on and the valve is shut.
Valve opens with a carton at the prox and the box not yet full.
rungs.condition: O:2/02 AND I:1/03 AND NOT I:1/04

rungs.description: FULL lamp follows the level sensor.

faults.effect: Drive roller lagging is worn smooth and the take-up is slack. The contactor pulls in and the gearmotor turns, but the belt slips on the drive roller and the carton never moves. Because no carton ever reaches the prox sensor, the fill never starts — so the PLC sits in a perfectly valid state, waiting.
clues: RUN lamp is lit and the motor is audibly running, but no carton moves.
O:2/00 is TRUE at the processor and 24 V is present at the contactor coil — the output is doing its job.
I:1/03 never makes, so FILL and FULL never light. The ladder is behaving exactly as written.
Belt surface is glazed; a hand mark on the belt does not travel with the drive roller.
Fine black rubber dust under the drive end of the conveyor.
faults.solution: Lock out and tag out the conveyor at the MCC before reaching inside the guard. Re-tension the belt at the take-up and replace the worn drive-roller lagging. This is a mechanical failure — no program or wiring change is correct.

redHerrings.description: The prox sensor's LED is dark.
redHerrings.location: Prox sensor bracket at the fill position
redHerrings.whyMisleading: It is dark because no target is in front of it, which is correct. Replacing a healthy sensor costs time and a parts-order penalty.

redHerrings.description: The level sensor lens has a light film of product dust.
redHerrings.whyMisleading: Real but irrelevant — the level sensor is downstream of the failure and is never reached this cycle. Cleaning it changes nothing.

derekScript.initialCall: The silo line's dead in the water. Motor's running, nothing's moving. I need cartons filling before the morning run.
derekScript.checkIn5min: Any joy? The RUN light's on, so it can't be the PLC, can it?
derekScript.impatient10min: We're backing up here. Just swap the sensor and let's move on.
derekScript.angry15min: This is costing us. If you can't find it I'm calling the contractor.
derekScript.resolution: Belt was slipping? All that and it's a roller. Good catch — better than the contractor would've done.
